name: Tsiolkovsky's Space Tower, 1895
description: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky's idea of a tower rising from the Earth's surface to geostationary height, so that a payload could reach orbit without rockets.
failedFuture: A way to climb out of gravity by stairs instead of fire. The tower was never built, but the same idea, a cable from the ground to orbit, still drives space-elevator studies.

name: Project Habbakuk, 1942–1943
description: A British plan, promoted by Geoffrey Pyke, for an enormous aircraft carrier built from Pykrete, a mix of ice and wood pulp. A 60-foot scale model was tested; the project was abandoned in 1943.
failedFuture: A carrier made of frozen water, cheap and hard to sink. The model was built and tested, but the war changed and the need disappeared. It survives as a case of wartime invention that never reached the sea.
source: National Interest, "Project Habakkuk: Churchill's Plan for an Aircraft Carrier Made of Ice".

failedFuture: A bomber that would have crossed the ocean at the edge of space. The war ended before it flew; afterwards its design became a reference for later spaceplane studies.
